why: A is the tail of the transform workbench's panel template (dim-preview banner, output viewer, layout report, bundle pane) while B is the middle of the here-view template (item header with prev/next and a swipe strip of cards), so they render unrelated UIs.

A reads a pivot cache's records out of the parsed workbook and returns rows with total, declared and truncated, while B calls A and reshapes the result into a labelled entry with a note when the counts disagree, so B consumes A and cannot replace it.

A is an after-callback in the transform workbench that defers work to a animation frame, while B is a debounced scroll listener in the swipe deck that clears an aim target after 160ms; the shared requestAnimationFrame wrapper is the only likeness.

A is a scroll handler that finds the slide whose bounding rect is nearest the strip's left edge and stores it in this.at, while B is a pure getter that returns the index by rounding scrollLeft over clientWidth (full-width cards only); they compute the same quantity but one assigns state and the other returns a value.

A profiles one column of tabular rows (types, null count, distinct values with a cap), while B analyzes a whole JSON document (node count, depth, type counts, top-level collections) and infers a per-column schema only for record arrays, so they overlap on column typing but neither could stand in for the other.
